metadata.title: Energy Market Operations Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the product, customer, connection, contract, billing, payment, portal, meter-data, allocation, forecasting, nomination, intraday, settlement, trading, market-data, market-message, reporting and platform data assets that power the energy market lifecycle (Propose, Onboard, Measure, Bill, Serve, Source, Forecast, Nominate, Steer, Settle) on the consolidated Energy21 + Ecedo + Jules + Gridhub + Nemon platform, with classification, GDPR/AVG and smart-meter governance, Dutch and Iberian energy-market, fiscal, balancing and wholesale-market obligations, backing stores, and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Supplier Data
rootGroups.description: What an energy supplier sells, to whom, at which connection, under which contract, and how it is billed, paid and served: the proposition and tariff catalogue, campaigns and B2B quotes, customer accounts, EAN/CUPS connection points and switch requests, supply contracts, invoices, corrections, payments and debtor cases, and the portal accounts, service cases and communications through which 7 million households and 3 million business customers of Dutch supplier clients meet their supplier. Almost every asset here is personal data under GDPR/AVG and is subject to Dutch (ACM, Energiewet, Belastingdienst) or Spanish and Portuguese (CNMC, ERSE) supply and fiscal rules.

subGroups.name: Products and Pricing
subGroups.description: The commercial catalogue that the proposition builder configures and that the order-to-cash backbone executes: products and tariffs, campaigns and channel availability, and cost-plus quotes for business customers.

assets.name: Energy Product and Tariff
assets.description: A sellable energy proposition of a supplier tenant and its versioned tariff structure: product type (fixed, variable, dynamic spot-indexed, EV time-of-use, battery or solar bundle, capacity-linked, multi-site B2B framework), commodity (electricity, gas, heat) and segment, tariff components per commodity (supply rate per kWh or m3 per tariff period, standing charge, purchase and imbalance surcharges, energy-tax brackets with the annual tax reduction per connection (the Dutch ODE levy is part of the energy tax since 1 January 2023), VAT treatment, 2023 price-cap and ACM model-contract flags), dynamic-pricing formula against the day-ahead index in 15-minute or hourly blocks, contract duration, termination fee rules, guarantee-of-origin source and label, eligibility rules per connection type, validity windows, and the customer-journey and document templates bound to it. Configured in Proposition and Tariff Builder (prod), exposed to channels by Campaign and Sales Channel Management (camp), priced from Price Curves and Market Data (pric), and executed downstream by contracts, billing and the portal without re-keying.
assets.businessMeaning: The thing that decides time to launch: a proposition that is configured once and flows automatically into contracts, billing, market communication and the portal is what turns eighteen months into weeks.
assets.accessScope: product, pricing and marketing staff of the owning supplier tenant; published tariff sheets and price-cap disclosures are public per ACM and CNMC rules; portal and channels see only active, eligible products

interfaces.name: product and tariff api
interfaces.description: Product, tariff version, eligibility and dynamic-pricing formula API with effective-dated lookups per connection type and date, used by the proposition builder, channels, quoting, contracts, billing runs, the customer portal and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: product lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Product published, tariff version activated, price-cap or energy-tax band changed, product withdrawn and campaign-eligibility changed events consumed by campaigns, contracts, billing, the portal and customer communication.

governance.retention: every tariff version kept for as long as any contract references it and 7 years after the last invoice under Dutch fiscal retention, because a disputed invoice must be recomputable against the tariff that applied; withdrawn products archived, never deleted
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; published tariffs and mandatory price disclosures are public; propositions never shared between tenants; anonymised product-type mix may feed cross-tenant market benchmarks

assets.name: Campaign
assets.description: A commercial campaign of a supplier tenant and its channel configuration: campaign identity and period, promoted products and tariff versions, discount or welcome-bonus rules, sales-channel availability (own website, white-label portal, price-comparison sites, telesales, door-to-door, partner and broker channels) with channel-specific journeys and cooling-off handling, target segments and eligibility filters, promo codes and attribution keys, lead and sign-up counts per channel and day, conversion to contract, cost per acquisition, and the compliance checklist (ACM information duty, model contract, welcome-bonus disclosure). Configured and tracked in Campaign and Sales Channel Management (camp) on top of the product catalogue.
assets.businessMeaning: Where propositions meet the market: the campaign decides which channels can sell what, from when, at which conditions, and reports the conversion that the proposition manager is judged on.
assets.accessScope: marketing, sales and product staff of the owning supplier tenant; channel partners see only their own channel's campaign parameters and attribution results; lead-level records restricted to sales and onboarding staff

interfaces.name: campaign and channel api
interfaces.description: Campaign, channel availability, promo-code validation and attribution API used by the sales channels, intake flows, the white-label portal sign-up journey, comparison-site feeds and dashboards.

interfaces.name: campaign events
interfaces.description: Campaign started, channel opened or closed, lead captured, sign-up attributed and campaign ended events consumed by intake, dashboards and customer communication.

governance.retention: campaign configuration kept 7 years with the contracts it produced; lead records of prospects who never became customers deleted 12 months after the campaign ends under GDPR storage limitation unless marketing consent is on file
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; attribution results shared with the channel partner that generated them; never shared between tenants

assets.name: B2B Quote
assets.description: A priced offer for a business or multi-site customer: the requesting organisation and contacts, the EAN or CUPS connection points in scope with their profile categories, capacity and historical consumption, the offered product structure (fixed, tranche or click, spot-indexed, cost-plus with pass-through of grid, tax and imbalance costs), price components derived from the forward curve at quote time (baseload and peak prices per delivery period, shape and profile cost, imbalance and volume-risk premium, margin), volume tolerance bands and take-or-pay terms, guarantee-of-origin options, validity window and price-lock expiry, approval status against mandate limits, and the accepted version that becomes the supply contract. Created in B2B Quoting and Cost-Plus Pricing (quot) from price curves and consumption profiles.
assets.businessMeaning: Where portfolio cost meets the customer: a quote priced from a stale curve or a wrong profile is margin given away for years, so every quote must trace back to the curve and consumption it was priced on.
assets.accessScope: B2B sales, pricing desk and portfolio staff of the owning supplier tenant within their mandate limits; the requesting customer sees its own offers through the customer-trading portal; brokers see only quotes they mediated

interfaces.name: b2b quote api
interfaces.description: Create, price, re-price, approve, expire and accept API for multi-site quotes with curve snapshot and profile references, used by the quoting workspace, the customer-trading desk, contracts and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: quote events
interfaces.description: Quote priced, approval requested, price-lock expiring, quote accepted or rejected events consumed by contracts, portfolio position tracking, workflow and dashboards.

governance.retention: accepted quotes kept with the contract for the contract term plus 7 years under Dutch fiscal retention; rejected or expired quotes kept 24 months for pricing analysis then anonymised
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; shared with the quoted customer and its mandated broker; price build-up internal to the pricing desk; never shared between tenants

subGroups.name: Customers and Connections
subGroups.description: Who the supplier serves and where energy is delivered: the customer account, the EAN or CUPS connection point registered with the grid operator, and the switch or move-in request that binds them through market communication.

assets.name: Customer Account
assets.description: The single customer record of a supplier tenant: household or business identity (name, date of birth or KvK/CIF number, contact details, correspondence and delivery addresses, preferred language), authorised representatives and contacts, identity-verification and credit-check outcome, payment method and SEPA mandate reference, invoicing preferences, communication consents and marketing opt-ins, vulnerability and protected-customer flags (payment arrangement, disconnection protection, bono social eligibility in Spain), linked connection points and contracts, lifecycle state (prospect, active, moving, terminated) and the merge history from heritage Ecedo, Gridhub and Nemon CRM records. Created by Intake, Credit Check and Activation (intk), maintained in Contracts and Connections Register (cntr), used by Customer Service Case Management (care), Customer Communication and Documents (comm) and Migration and Platform Consolidation Tooling (migr).
assets.businessMeaning: Where GDPR obligations begin and where cost to serve is decided: one clean customer record shared by billing, portal and care is the precondition for self-service and for a bill the customer trusts.
assets.accessScope: onboarding, billing and customer-service staff of the owning supplier tenant; each customer sees and edits its own account in the portal; vulnerability flags visible only to care and debtor staff; grid operators receive only the attributes market messages require

interfaces.name: customer account api
interfaces.description: Create, verify, search, update, consent and merge API for customer accounts with role-based field masking, used by intake, contracts, billing, care, communication, the portal, migration tooling and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: customer lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Customer created, identity verified, address or payment method changed, consent changed, vulnerability flag set, customer terminated and erasure requested events consumed by contracts, billing, the portal, communication and market-message processing.

governance.retention: kept for the supply relationship plus 7 years after the last invoice under Dutch fiscal retention (6 years under the Spanish Código de Comercio (4 years for tax) and 10 years in Portugal); identity-verification evidence kept only as long as the check needs to be demonstrable; prospects that never contracted deleted after 12 months; GDPR erasure honoured by pseudonymising the account while keeping fiscal records
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; shared with grid operators, metering companies and the central connection register only as market messages require; shared with payment and collection providers for their processing; never shared between tenants or with the platform operator's other clients

assets.name: Connection Point
assets.description: A physical grid connection as known in the central register: the 18-digit EAN (one per commodity) in the Netherlands or the 20-22-character CUPS (ES or PT prefix) in Spain and Portugal, commodity and address, grid operator and grid area, connection category (small consumer, large consumer, production, BSP or flex asset), allocation method under Allocation 2.0 (TMT, SMA or PRO), profile category (E1A-E4A, G1A-G2C) and capacity code, the Iberian access tariff (2.0TD, 3.0TD, 6.xTD) with contracted power per period, physical capacity and contracted transport capacity, tariff-area and tax-band attributes, meter number, type and smart-meter administrative status (on, administratively off, read consent), installed production (solar, CHP, battery) and net-metering status, the current supplier, BRP and metering responsible party per date, and the mirrored history from the EDSN central connection register (C-AR) or the Iberian distributor SIPS files. Read and validated by Intake, Credit Check and Activation (intk), transferred through Switching and Move-In Market Processes (swch), held in Contracts and Connections Register (cntr), keyed by Meter Data Collection and Validation (mdat) and mirrored through Dutch Market Messaging Hub (mcom) and Iberian Market Communication (imcm).
assets.businessMeaning: The spine of the market: every switch, meter reading, allocation volume, invoice and nomination resolves to a connection point and a date range, and the register decides who may bill and who is balance-responsible.
assets.accessScope: onboarding, billing, meter-data and market-communication staff of the owning supplier or BRP tenant; a customer sees only its own connections in the portal; grid operators and metering parties exchange attributes per market process; the central register is the external master

interfaces.name: connection point api
interfaces.description: EAN and CUPS lookup, register query, attribute history, capacity and profile-category API used by intake, switching, contracts, meter data, allocation, nominations, the portal and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: connection register events
interfaces.description: Supplier or BRP assignment changed, meter replaced, smart-meter status changed, capacity or profile category changed, production installed and connection removed events consumed by contracts, billing, meter data, allocation and forecasting.

interfaces.name: central register synchronisation files
interfaces.description: Daily C-AR delta files from EDSN and distributor SIPS extract files from Spain and Portugal landed and reconciled against the local mirror.

governance.retention: attribute history kept for the supply relationship plus 7 years because allocation disputes, reconciliation and fiscal audits are resolved per connection and period; the external central register is authoritative for current state
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with grid operators, TSOs, metering parties, the central register and the BRP as market processes require; a supplier tenant sees only connections it supplies or has a pending switch for; never shared between tenants beyond what the market process discloses

assets.name: Switch Request
assets.description: A market process instance that moves a connection to the supplier or changes its state: process type (supplier switch, move-in, move-out, end of supply, contract change, BRP change, meter-reading request, master-data correction), the connection point and customer, requested and effective dates, the sequence of market messages sent and received with their EDSN process names (leverancierswissel, inhuizing, uithuizing, einde levering, PV-wissel) or Iberian ATR request types (C1, C2, A3, B1, M1), gain and loss acknowledgements, rejection reasons and retry state, cooling-off cancellations (the losing supplier cannot object in the Dutch process), the meter readings exchanged at the switch date, the losing or gaining supplier, the linked contract activation, and SLA timers against the ACM and CNMC switching terms. Orchestrated by Switching and Move-In Market Processes (swch) over the market-message hubs.
assets.businessMeaning: The moment a customer becomes a customer: a switch that fails or stalls costs the sale, breaches the switching deadline and creates the first correction on the first invoice.
assets.accessScope: onboarding and market-communication staff of the owning supplier tenant; the customer sees the status of its own switch or move in the portal; the counterparty supplier and grid operator see only the market messages of the process

interfaces.name: switch request api
interfaces.description: Start, track, cancel, retry and query API for switch, move-in, move-out and contract-change processes with SLA status, used by intake, contracts, the portal, care and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: switch process events
interfaces.description: Switch requested, accepted, rejected, cooling-off cancellation received, effective date reached, meter reading received and process completed events consumed by contracts, billing, the portal, communication and workflow exceptions.

governance.retention: process records and message trail kept 7 years because disputes about switch dates, readings and cancellations are settled between suppliers and grid operators long after the event; open processes never purged
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; exchanged with grid operators, the central register and the counterparty supplier through market messages only; never shared between tenants otherwise

subGroups.name: Contracts and Billing
subGroups.description: The order-to-cash core: the supply contract, the invoices produced by billing runs, the corrections and re-billing that reconciliation triggers, the payments and direct debits that settle them, and the debtor cases when they do not.

assets.name: Supply Contract
assets.description: The agreement under which a supplier delivers energy to a customer at one or more connection points: contract type and product version, per-connection commodity, start and end dates, price components fixed at signature or indexed per period, price-cap and model-contract applicability, tranche or click schedule for B2B framework contracts, volume bands and take-or-pay terms, guarantee-of-origin allocation, advance-payment amount and reset rules, billing frequency and invoice grouping (split invoicing per site, consolidated invoices per organisation), termination and renewal terms with fee rules, signed document and e-signature evidence, amendments and price-change notifications, and contract state from offer to termination. Created by Intake, Credit Check and Activation (intk), held in Contracts and Connections Register (cntr), billed by Billing Runs and Invoicing (bill) and extended with executed trades by Customer Trading Desk and Click Contracts (ctrd).
assets.businessMeaning: The legal and financial truth of every connection: what price applies to which volume in which period, and therefore the basis of every invoice, margin figure and dispute.
assets.accessScope: contract, billing and care staff of the owning supplier tenant; the customer sees its own contracts, prices and documents in the portal; brokers and industrial energy managers see the framework contracts they are mandated for; auditors and ACM or CNMC on request

interfaces.name: supply contract api
interfaces.description: Create, activate, amend, price-change, renew and terminate API with effective-dated price and connection lookups, used by intake, switching, billing, customer trading, the portal, care, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: contract lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Contract signed, activated, price changed, advance amount reset, tranche clicked, renewal due, terminated and ended events consumed by billing, payments, forecasting, portfolio position, communication and the portal.

governance.retention: kept for the contract term plus 7 years after the final settlement under Dutch fiscal retention and 6 years under the Spanish Código de Comercio (4 years for tax) and 10 years in Portugal; signed documents and e-signature evidence kept as long as the contract can be contested
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; shared with the customer and its mandated broker; contract prices feed portfolio position and forecasting inside the same tenant; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Invoice
assets.description: A billing document produced by a billing run: advance, periodic, annual settlement, final settlement, correction or credit note; per connection and period the volumes billed (validated readings, allocated or estimated volumes, production and net-metering or feed-in compensation), the tariff components applied, energy tax per bracket and the annual tax reduction (ODE included since 2023), the Spanish Impuesto Especial sobre la Electricidad, VAT per rate, guarantees of origin, grid and metering charges passed through, the advance payments settled, the amount due and due date, payment method and mandate, the invoice specification and PDF, the delivery channel and date, and reversal or correction links. Generated by Billing Runs and Invoicing (bill), corrected through Billing Reconciliation and Corrections (recn), settled by Payments, Direct Debit and Debtor Management (paym) and shown with its breakdown in the White-Label Customer Portal and App (port).
assets.businessMeaning: The one artefact every end customer judges the supplier by, the driver of straight-through billing rate and correction rate, and a fiscal document that must be reproducible for seven years.
assets.accessScope: billing, debtor and care staff of the owning supplier tenant; each customer sees its own invoices and specifications in the portal; accounting and payment providers receive ledger and collection extracts; tax authorities and auditors on request

interfaces.name: invoice api
interfaces.description: Invoice run, preview, issue, specification, PDF, reversal and status API used by billing runs, reconciliation, payments, the portal, care, accounting connectors and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: invoice events
interfaces.description: Invoice issued, delivered, due, paid, overdue, reversed and credited events consumed by payments, debtor management, communication, the portal, dashboards and accounting.

interfaces.name: invoice and ledger exports
interfaces.description: Batch exports of issued invoices, VAT summaries and sub-ledger journals to ERP and accounting systems and to e-invoicing channels for business customers.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of issue under Dutch fiscal retention (Belastingdienst, AWR art. 52), 6 years under the Spanish Código de Comercio (4 years for tax) and 10 years in Portugal; underlying volumes and tariff versions kept with the invoice so any invoice can be recomputed
governance.sharingPolicy: each customer receives only its own invoices; shared with the tenant's accounting system, payment and collection providers and, for business customers, their e-invoicing platform; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Billing Correction
assets.description: A detected and resolved billing exception: the trigger (late or corrected meter reading, allocation or reconciliation volume differing from billed volume, tariff or tax-band misapplication, master-data change with retroactive effect, switch-date dispute, customer complaint), the connection, period and invoices affected, the original and recomputed volumes and amounts, the correction rule that classified it, the decision to re-bill, credit or absorb, the reviewer and approval state, the resulting credit note or corrective invoice, the root-cause code, and the age of the exception against the tenant's service levels. Produced and managed by Billing Reconciliation and Corrections (recn) by comparing invoices with allocation volumes and readings.
assets.businessMeaning: The measure of the operation: corrections are what stand between the billing run and straight-through billing, and their root causes tell the operations manager where the data is wrong.
assets.accessScope: billing operations and reconciliation staff of the owning supplier tenant; care staff see corrections on the cases they handle; the customer sees only the resulting credit note or corrective invoice

interfaces.name: billing correction api
interfaces.description: Detect, classify, recompute, approve, re-bill and close API with root-cause coding, used by the reconciliation workspace, billing runs, care, workflow exceptions and dashboards.

interfaces.name: correction events
interfaces.description: Exception detected, correction approved, credit note issued, correction absorbed and exception aged events consumed by billing, payments, care, workflow and the straight-through billing dashboards.

governance.retention: kept with the corrected invoice 7 years under fiscal retention; root-cause statistics kept indefinitely in anonymised form
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; only the resulting documents are shared with the customer; anonymised root-cause rates may feed cross-tenant billing-quality benchmarks

assets.name: Payment Transaction
assets.description: A movement of money between a customer and the supplier tenant: SEPA Core direct-debit collections (pain.008) generated from advance and settlement invoices with mandate reference, creditor identifier and pre-notification date, incoming transfers and iDEAL or card payments matched to invoices by reference and amount, refunds of credit balances, chargebacks and rejected debits with reason codes, payment-plan instalments, allocations across open items, bank-statement lines imported from the tenant's bank or PSP, unmatched or partially matched items, and the resulting customer balance per date. Processed by Payments, Direct Debit and Debtor Management (paym) against invoices and pushed to the tenant's accounting system.
assets.businessMeaning: Cash: the difference between invoiced and collected is working capital and bad debt, and matching without manual work is the last step of straight-through billing.
assets.accessScope: debtor, treasury and billing staff of the owning supplier tenant; the customer sees its own payments and balance in the portal; bank and PSP connectors exchange only their own transactions; IBANs masked outside the payments module

interfaces.name: payment api
interfaces.description: Direct-debit batch, payment matching, refund, payment-plan and balance API used by billing, debtor management, the portal, care, bank and PSP connectors and accounting.

interfaces.name: payment events
interfaces.description: Debit collected, debit rejected, payment received, payment matched, refund issued and balance changed events consumed by debtor management, the portal, communication and dashboards.

interfaces.name: sepa and bank statement files
interfaces.description: SEPA pain.008 direct-debit batches sent to the bank, pain.002 rejections and camt.053 statements imported daily, and PSP settlement reports.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year under Dutch fiscal retention; SEPA mandates kept while valid and at least 14 months after the last collection per the SDD Core rulebook (a mandate lapses after 36 months without a collection); an authorised debit can be reclaimed for 8 weeks, an unauthorised one for 13 months; bank statement files kept with the ledger
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the tenant's bank, PSP and accounting system for processing; the customer sees its own transactions; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Debtor Case
assets.description: The collection and credit-management history of a customer with overdue amounts: open items and ageing, dunning stage and letters sent with statutory reminder terms and costs, payment arrangements and their adherence, the protected-customer assessment (vulnerable household, the 1 October-1 April winter period of the Dutch Regeling afsluitbeleid, medical dependency, bono social in Spain) that governs whether disconnection may be requested, referral to debt assistance under the Dutch early-signalling duty, the disconnection request to the grid operator and its reversal on payment, handover to an external collection agency or bailiff with the file transferred, credit-scoring inputs at intake, write-off and bad-debt provisioning, and the case timeline. Managed by Payments, Direct Debit and Debtor Management (paym).
assets.businessMeaning: Where cost to serve, bad debt and regulatory exposure meet: a wrongly escalated case is a disconnection complaint and an ACM finding, a case escalated too late is a write-off.
assets.accessScope: debtor-management and care staff of the owning supplier tenant; medical and vulnerability information restricted to named debtor staff; collection agencies receive only the handed-over file; the customer sees its arrangements and open items in the portal

interfaces.name: debtor case api
interfaces.description: Ageing, dunning stage, arrangement, protection assessment, disconnection request, agency handover and write-off API used by the debtor workspace, care, the portal, market-message processing and dashboards.

interfaces.name: debtor case events
interfaces.description: Case opened, reminder sent, arrangement agreed or broken, early-signalling referral made, disconnection requested or reversed, case handed over and case closed events consumed by communication, workflow, market messaging and dashboards.

governance.retention: case records kept 7 years after closure with the invoices they concern; vulnerability and medical indications deleted as soon as the protection they justify has lapsed; agency handover files returned or destroyed at contract end
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the grid operator only as a disconnection or reconnection request, with municipalities under the early-signalling duty and with the mandated collection agency; never shared between tenants

subGroups.name: Customer Interfacing
subGroups.description: How end customers meet their supplier on the same data as billing: the portal or app account, the service cases raised by customers and staff, and every message and document sent.

assets.name: Portal Account
assets.description: The digital identity of an end customer, business user or partner on the white-label portal and app of a supplier tenant: login credentials or federated identity, multi-factor settings, the brand and tenant the account belongs to, the customer accounts and connections the user may see (household, multi-site business, energy manager acting for an organisation, broker mandate), role and consent scope, notification preferences and push tokens, session and device history, portal usage and self-service task completion signals, and account state (invited, active, locked, closed). Owned by the White-Label Customer Portal and App (port), which creates accounts, mandates and preferences; authenticated and isolated per brand through Identity, Tenants and Brand Isolation (iden).
assets.businessMeaning: The gate to self-service: only an account that is secure, correctly scoped to the right connections and easy to recover lets a customer serve itself instead of calling.
assets.accessScope: the account holder; identity administrators of the platform operator for support and security operations; care staff of the owning supplier tenant see account state but never credentials

interfaces.name: portal account and identity api
interfaces.description: Registration, authentication (OIDC), mandate and scope, notification-preference and account-recovery API used by the portal and app, care, communication and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: portal account events
interfaces.description: Account activated, login anomaly, mandate granted or revoked, preference changed and account closed events consumed by care, communication and security monitoring.

governance.retention: kept while the customer relationship lasts; closed 24 months after the last contract ends or on erasure request; authentication logs kept 12 months for security investigation
governance.sharingPolicy: never shared beyond the account holder and the owning tenant's care staff; federated identity providers receive only the identifiers needed to authenticate; strict isolation between brands and tenants

assets.name: Service Case
assets.description: A customer request, question, complaint or dispute and its resolution: the channel it arrived through (portal, app, e-mail, phone, chat, letter, comparison-site, ACM ConsuWijzer or CNMC referral), the customer, connection and invoice or process it concerns, the case category (invoice dispute, meter reading, switch or move, payment arrangement, tariff change, supply interruption, data request, complaint), priority and statutory response terms, the context snapshot from billing, meter data and market processes at the time of the case, actions and notes, escalation to a formal complaint or the Geschillencommissie or the Iberian consumer arbitration, linked corrections and communications, resolution code and customer satisfaction score. Managed by Customer Service Case Management (care).
assets.businessMeaning: Where contact rate and self-service resolution are measured, and the only place the supplier learns what its bill and its data got wrong.
assets.accessScope: care and back-office staff of the owning supplier tenant; the customer sees its own cases and their status in the portal; dispute bodies receive the case file for escalated complaints

interfaces.name: service case api
interfaces.description: Create, classify, assign, contextualise, escalate, resolve and rate API with omnichannel intake, used by the care workspace, the portal and app, communication, billing corrections and dashboards.

interfaces.name: service case events
interfaces.description: Case opened, assigned, response term approaching, escalated, resolved and rated events consumed by workflow, communication, corrections and contact-rate dashboards.

governance.retention: kept 5 years after closure so recurring complaints and escalations can be reviewed, longer where linked to an invoice under fiscal retention; call recordings and chat transcripts kept 12 months
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the supplier tenant; shared with the customer and with dispute bodies for escalated cases; anonymised case categories may feed cross-tenant contact-rate benchmarks

assets.name: Customer Communication
assets.description: Every outbound and inbound message and document between a supplier tenant and its customers: welcome and contract confirmation, price-change and price-cap notifications with statutory notice periods, annual settlement and invoice delivery, meter-reading requests, switch and move confirmations, dunning letters, tariff-comparison and consumption reports, regulatory disclosures (fuel mix, complaint procedure, model-contract offer), campaign and service e-mails, SMS and push notifications, letters and their print-house batches, template and brand version used, delivery channel, timestamp and delivery status, opt-out state, and inbound scans and e-mails linked to cases. Generated and archived by Customer Communication and Documents (comm) from templates bound to products and journeys.
assets.businessMeaning: The evidence of having informed the customer: notice periods, price changes and disclosures are legal obligations that must be proven, and communication that is timely and clear is what keeps customers from calling and from leaving.
assets.accessScope: care, billing and marketing staff of the owning supplier tenant; each customer sees its own documents and messages in the portal; print and e-mail providers process batches under processor agreements

interfaces.name: communication and document api
interfaces.description: Template rendering, multi-channel send, delivery status, document retrieval and inbound-linking API used by billing, contracts, switching, debtor management, care, the portal and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: communication events
interfaces.description: Message queued, sent, delivered, bounced, opened and opted out events consumed by care, campaigns, workflow and dashboards.

interfaces.name: print and e-mail batches
interfaces.description: Daily letter batches to print houses and bulk e-mail or SMS batches to messaging providers with delivery reports imported back.

governance.retention: contractual and statutory notifications kept 7 years with the contract and invoice they concern; marketing communications and delivery logs kept 24 months; inbound scans kept with the case
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with print, e-mail and SMS processors under processor agreements; the customer sees its own history; never shared between tenants

rootGroups.name: Balancing Data
rootGroups.description: What actually flowed and what the balance responsible party promised: meter readings and 15-minute interval data from smart meters, telemetry and clustered profiles; allocation and reconciliation volumes per BRP, grid area and period under Allocation 2.0; forecasts and nominations to TenneT and the gas TSOs; near real-time intraday positions and steering signals; and the imbalance settlement per imbalance settlement period. This is the data on which the platform validates over 90% of Dutch energy consumption data and runs BRP as a Service; household interval data is personal data under GDPR and Dutch smart-meter rules, while positions and nominations are commercially critical and essential-entity infrastructure under NIS2.

subGroups.name: Meter Data and Allocation
subGroups.description: Measured volumes per connection and interval, and the market's official accounting of who supplied what: allocation per BRP and grid area, and its later reconciliation against actual readings.

assets.name: Meter Reading
assets.description: Measured energy per connection point and time: register readings (cumulative kWh or m3 per tariff register, at switch, move, annual and ad-hoc dates; customer-submitted, estimated or metering-party readings) and interval series (15-minute electricity and hourly gas values from smart meters requested through the grid operators' P4 channel (daily standard readings for every smart meter, household interval data only with the customer's consent) or delivered by the metering responsible party, hourly curves from the Iberian distributors' P1/P2 measurement files, telemetry from large-consumer and production meters, clustered and profiled data for connections without interval reads, feed-in and production registers), each with source, quality flag (measured, estimated, substituted, plausibility-checked, corrected), validation rule outcomes, gaps and interpolations, temperature and profile-category context, and the version history as later readings replace estimates. Collected and validated by Meter Data Collection and Validation (mdat), consumed by Billing Runs and Invoicing (bill), Allocation and Reconciliation (allo), the White-Label Customer Portal and App (port) and Consumption Analysis and Forecast Self-Service (cons).
assets.businessMeaning: The physical truth behind every invoice, allocation and forecast; reading data that is validated once and reused by billing, portal and settlement is why the customer, the BRP and the grid operator see the same number.
assets.accessScope: meter-data, billing and care staff of the owning supplier or BRP tenant; a household sees its own readings and consumption in the portal; fine-grained smart-meter interval data collected only with the customer's consent or for the legally permitted billing purpose; grid operators and metering parties exchange readings through market processes

interfaces.name: meter reading api
interfaces.description: Register reading submit and validate, interval series query per EAN or CUPS and period with quality flags, estimation and correction API used by billing, allocation, the portal, consumption analysis, forecasting, care and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: meter data events
interfaces.description: Reading received, interval batch validated, gap detected, estimate replaced by measurement and reading corrected events consumed by billing, corrections, allocation, forecasting and the portal.

interfaces.name: meter data delivery files
interfaces.description: Daily P4 and metering-party interval deliveries, telemetry feeds and Iberian distributor measurement files landed, parsed and validated into the time-series store.

governance.retention: readings underlying invoices kept 7 years under fiscal retention; household 15-minute interval data kept only as long as billing, allocation disputes and the customer's own insight require and aggregated to daily values afterwards under Dutch smart-meter privacy rules; consent withdrawal stops fine-grained collection
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with grid operators, metering parties, the BRP and TenneT through market processes only; the customer sees and can export its own data; validated and aggregated consumption may be provided to grid operators as a data product; never shared between tenants at connection level

assets.name: Allocation Volume
assets.description: The market's official attribution of energy per imbalance settlement period: for each BRP, grid area, supplier and profile category the allocated volumes per 15-minute imbalance settlement period (electricity) or hour (gas) as computed by the grid operators per allocation method (TMT telemetered, SMA smart-meter quarter-hour data, PRO profiled) and published through EDSN and, for the reconciliation data, the TenneT market-to-market communication hub (MMC-Hub) under Allocation 2.0, the platform's shadow allocation from its own validated volumes, the allocation version (preliminary, definitive, corrected) and publication date, the Iberian equivalent settlement measures per distributor and REE, the comparison with the tenant's own aggregated meter data and the resulting deviation per grid area and segment. Received and processed by Allocation and Reconciliation (allo), reconciled with invoices by Billing Reconciliation and Corrections (recn) and settled by Imbalance Settlement and BRP Compliance (imbs).
assets.businessMeaning: The volume the BRP is charged for: allocation decides the imbalance invoice from TenneT, and its match with billed volumes decides whether the supplier bought what it sold.
assets.accessScope: allocation, settlement and portfolio staff of the owning BRP or supplier tenant; the BRP-as-a-Service desk of the platform operator for managed portfolios; grid operators and TenneT are the external source

interfaces.name: allocation volume api
interfaces.description: Allocation query per BRP, grid area, supplier, segment and period with version and deviation, used by reconciliation, imbalance settlement, billing corrections, portfolio position, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: allocation events
interfaces.description: Allocation published, version superseded, deviation threshold exceeded and allocation period closed events consumed by settlement, corrections, portfolio position and dashboards.

interfaces.name: allocation message files
interfaces.description: Daily and monthly allocation and reconciliation messages from EDSN and the MMC-Hub, and REE and distributor settlement files for Iberia, archived as received.

governance.retention: kept 7 years with the settlement and invoices it underpins; every version kept because reconciliation and disputes refer to specific allocation versions
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with grid operators, TenneT and the BRP through market processes; a supplier tenant sees allocations of its own connections and the aggregate of the BRP it belongs to; never shared between BRP tenants

assets.name: Reconciliation Volume
assets.description: The correction of allocated volumes once actual readings are known: per BRP, supplier, grid area, profile category and month the difference between the profiled allocation and the measured consumption of profiled connections, the reconciliation runs at the statutory intervals (the monthly and the final reconciliation after the 17-month window in the Dutch market), the Allocation 2.0 reconciliation for small-consumer and telemetered connections exchanged via the MMC-Hub since 1 January 2025, the reconciliation price per period, the resulting financial settlement between BRPs through TenneT, the per-connection contributions used to explain differences, and the version and publication date of each run. Computed and matched by Allocation and Reconciliation (allo) against allocation volumes and meter readings.
assets.businessMeaning: The final truth of the supplied volume: reconciliation turns estimates into money owed or owed back between BRPs and is where allocation reconciliation accuracy is measured.
assets.accessScope: allocation and settlement staff of the owning BRP or supplier tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk; TenneT and grid operators are the counterparties

interfaces.name: reconciliation volume api
interfaces.description: Reconciliation run, match, explain-by-connection and financial-result API used by allocation, billing corrections, imbalance settlement, dashboards and regulatory reporting.

interfaces.name: reconciliation events
interfaces.description: Reconciliation run received, matched, unexplained difference flagged and reconciliation settled events consumed by corrections, settlement, workflow and dashboards.

governance.retention: kept 7 years with the settlement it produced; all runs kept until the final reconciliation of the period has been settled and audited
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with TenneT, grid operators and the BRP; the supplier sees its own share; never shared between tenants

subGroups.name: Forecasting and Nomination
subGroups.description: What the portfolio is expected to consume and produce, and what has been promised to the TSO: day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasts per portfolio segment and the nominations and re-nominations to TenneT and the gas TSOs.

assets.name: Portfolio Forecast
assets.description: Expected consumption and production of a portfolio per 15-minute (electricity) or hourly (gas) period: the forecast horizon and run (day-ahead, intraday updates, ex-post reconstruction), the portfolio segment (household profiles, business profiles, interval-metered large consumers, solar, wind, CHP, batteries, EV charging, flex assets), the model and features used (temperature and irradiance forecasts, calendar, historical interval data, contract portfolio changes from switches and moves, customer-submitted forecasts), the forecast value with confidence bands, the weather and price scenario, the actual volume once known and the deviation, and the accuracy statistics per segment and horizon. Produced by Portfolio Forecasting (fcst) from consumption profiles and used by Nominations and Position Management (nomi).
assets.businessMeaning: The number the BRP nominates and hedges on: forecast accuracy per segment is the first lever on imbalance cost per MWh and the basis of the 15-minute financial insight per segment.
assets.accessScope: forecasting, trading and balancing staff of the owning BRP or portfolio tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk; large customers see forecasts of their own sites through the customer-trading portal

interfaces.name: portfolio forecast api
interfaces.description: Forecast run, query per portfolio, segment, horizon and period, scenario override and accuracy API used by nominations, position management, intraday steering, sourcing, customer trading, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: forecast events
interfaces.description: Day-ahead forecast published, intraday forecast updated, forecast deviation threshold exceeded and ex-post forecast closed events consumed by nominations, intraday steering, portfolio position and dashboards.

governance.retention: forecast runs kept 3 years for model evaluation and imbalance-dispute analysis; the day-ahead forecast used for each nomination kept 7 years with the settlement
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the portfolio tenant; site forecasts shared with the large customer they concern; anonymised segment accuracy may feed cross-tenant benchmarks; never shared between BRP tenants

assets.name: Nomination
assets.description: A binding energy programme submitted to a system operator: for electricity the E-programme to TenneT per BRP (identified by its EIC code) in MW per 15-minute imbalance settlement period of the delivery day, import and export per connection to other BRPs and cross-border, re-nominations up to gate closure, the acceptance or rejection response and the final approved programme; for gas the hourly nominations and re-nominations per network point and shipper code to GTS as Edig@s NOMINT messages with NOMRES responses (and the matching with EBN's shipping counterparties), the matching with the counterparty, and the confirmed quantities; each with the submission and gate-closure timestamps, the forecast and trades it was built from, the trader or automated cycle that submitted it, version history, and the mismatch and lateness statistics that feed nomination timeliness. Built and submitted by Nominations and Position Management (nomi), reused by Gas Shipping and Trading (gass) and compared with allocation by Imbalance Settlement and BRP Compliance (imbs).
assets.businessMeaning: The promise to the market: every deviation between nomination and allocation is imbalance cost, and a late or rejected nomination is a compliance incident with the TSO.
assets.accessScope: balancing and shipping staff of the owning BRP, shipper or portfolio tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk under four-eyes rules for manual submissions; TenneT, GTS and counterparties receive the programmes

interfaces.name: nomination api
interfaces.description: Build, validate, submit, re-nominate, status and history API for TenneT E-programmes and gas nominations, used by position management, intraday steering, gas shipping, settlement, the BRP operations desk and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: nomination events
interfaces.description: Nomination submitted, accepted, rejected, re-nominated, gate closure approaching and programme final events consumed by intraday steering, settlement, workflow alerts and dashboards.

interfaces.name: tso programme messages
interfaces.description: E-programme and gas nomination messages exchanged with TenneT and GTS over the TSO interfaces and archived with acknowledgements.

governance.retention: kept 7 years with the imbalance settlement under fiscal retention and 5 years for REMIT record-keeping; every version and acknowledgement kept for TSO audits
governance.sharingPolicy: submitted to TenneT, GTS and matching counterparties; visible only to the owning tenant and the managed-BRP desk that operates its portfolio; never shared between BRP tenants

subGroups.name: Intraday and Settlement
subGroups.description: The near real-time position of the portfolio, the signals that steer it, and the money the deviations cost: intraday positions, steering signals to traders and flex assets, and the imbalance settlement per imbalance settlement period.

assets.name: Intraday Position
assets.description: The near real-time balance of a portfolio for the current and coming imbalance settlement periods: the nominated volume, the latest intraday forecast per segment, real-time production and consumption telemetry from large sites, solar and wind assets and batteries, executed intraday trades on ETPA and EPEX, the resulting open position per 15 minutes, the TenneT imbalance price and regulation state signals, the expected imbalance cost or revenue per segment, position limits and alert thresholds, and the timeline of position updates during the delivery day. Maintained by Intraday Steering and Flex Signals (intr) as the input to steering decisions and the guaranteed intraday trading cycle.
assets.businessMeaning: The position the trader and the algorithm act on within the hour: seeing it per 15 minutes and per segment is what makes the claimed reduction of imbalance costs possible.
assets.accessScope: intraday traders and balancing operators of the owning BRP or portfolio tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk; large customers with flex assets see the position of their own assets

interfaces.name: intraday position api
interfaces.description: Position query per portfolio, segment and period with limits and expected cost, real-time telemetry ingest and position-update stream API used by the steering workspace, the intraday trading cycle, flex-asset controllers, risk analytics and dashboards.

interfaces.name: position update events
interfaces.description: Position recalculated, limit breached, imbalance price signal received and delivery period closed events consumed by steering signals, trading, alerts and dashboards.

governance.retention: position snapshots kept 3 years for steering evaluation and imbalance disputes; the final position per delivery day kept 7 years with the settlement
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the portfolio tenant; asset-level positions shared with the asset owner; never shared between tenants and never with exchanges beyond the trades placed

assets.name: Steering Signal
assets.description: An instruction or advisory generated from the intraday position: solar-optimised curtailment or production adjustment, battery charge and discharge setpoints, EV charging shifts, demand-response calls to curtailable industrial load, intraday buy or sell proposals for the ETPA and EPEX cycle, aFRR and passive-balancing opportunities in line with the TenneT 0.1 MW setpoint and 4-hour capacity auction regime, each with target asset or trader, delivery period, volume and price expectation, the position and price rationale, the automation level (advisory, auto-executed under supervision, executed), the acknowledgement or execution result from the asset controller or exchange, the resulting position effect, and the value captured per signal for flexibility-revenue reporting. Generated and dispatched by Intraday Steering and Flex Signals (intr).
assets.businessMeaning: Where imbalance cost is actually reduced and flexibility revenue is captured: the signal, its execution and its measured effect are the evidence for the value of steering.
assets.accessScope: balancing operators and traders of the owning tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk; asset controllers and industrial energy managers receive only signals for their own assets; auto-execution guarded by mandate limits

interfaces.name: steering signal api
interfaces.description: Signal generation, dispatch, acknowledgement, override and value-attribution API used by the steering workspace, flex-asset integrations, the intraday trading cycle, customer trading and dashboards.

interfaces.name: steering signal stream
interfaces.description: Signal issued, acknowledged, executed, rejected and effect measured events streamed to asset controllers, exchange connectors, position management and flexibility-revenue dashboards.

governance.retention: signals and execution results kept 3 years for steering evaluation and 5 years where they underlie REMIT-reportable orders; asset setpoint logs kept per the flex-asset contract
governance.sharingPolicy: dispatched only to the addressed asset controller, trader or exchange connector; asset owners see signals for their own assets; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Imbalance Settlement
assets.description: The financial consequence of deviating from the programme: per BRP and imbalance settlement period the difference between the approved nomination and the allocated volume, the TenneT imbalance price per regulation state and the resulting cost or revenue, the settlement statements and invoices from TenneT and their reconciliation with the platform's own computation, the gas balancing position and GTS cash-out, the reconciliation settlements between BRPs, the attribution of imbalance cost to portfolio segments and to managed-BRP clients for tiered per-MWh charging, the BRP compliance metrics (programme timeliness, deviation, reporting), and the dispute and correction trail with the TSO. Computed and reported by Imbalance Settlement and BRP Compliance (imbs) from nominations and allocation volumes.
assets.businessMeaning: The north-star number of the BRP operator: imbalance cost per MWh per segment, reconciled to the TSO invoice, is what BRP as a Service is judged and paid on.
assets.accessScope: settlement, finance and portfolio staff of the owning BRP or portfolio tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk; managed clients see the settlement of their own portfolio; TenneT and GTS are the counterparties

interfaces.name: imbalance settlement api
interfaces.description: Settlement computation, TSO invoice reconciliation, segment and client attribution, compliance metric and dispute API used by the settlement workspace, portfolio risk analytics, managed-BRP invoicing, regulatory reporting and dashboards.

interfaces.name: settlement events
interfaces.description: Settlement period computed, TSO invoice received, discrepancy flagged, dispute opened and settlement closed events consumed by accounting, workflow, risk analytics and dashboards.

interfaces.name: tso settlement files
interfaces.description: TenneT imbalance and reconciliation settlement files and GTS balancing statements imported and archived with the platform's reconciliation result.

governance.retention: 7 years under fiscal retention because settlements are invoiced and re-invoiced to managed clients; disputes kept until closed plus 7 years
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with TenneT and GTS; each managed client sees its own portfolio settlement; segment attribution internal to the tenant; never shared between BRP tenants

rootGroups.name: Trade and Portfolio Data
rootGroups.description: What the portfolio has bought and sold and what it is worth: hedge transactions on the wholesale markets, price curves from EPEX, OMIE and the forward markets, the consolidated portfolio position with value and risk per segment every 15 minutes, and the click trades and consumption profiles of business customers who trade through their supplier's platform. Wholesale-market data is commercially critical and REMIT-relevant; customer trades and site profiles carry the business customer's contact and consumption data.

subGroups.name: Sourcing and Portfolio
subGroups.description: The wholesale side of the supplier or portfolio operator: procurement and hedges, the market prices everything is valued against, and the resulting position, value and risk.

assets.name: Hedge Transaction
assets.description: A wholesale purchase or sale that sources or hedges the portfolio: OTC and exchange trades (EEX and ICE Endex futures, EPEX day-ahead and intraday, ETPA intraday, OMIE and MIBGAS for Iberia, TTF gas), PPAs with wind and solar producers, guarantee-of-origin purchases, and structured tranches, each with counterparty, product and delivery period, baseload or peak shape, volume in MW or MWh, price and currency, trade and settlement dates, the hedging strategy and portfolio segment it covers, confirmation and matching status, the credit and collateral impact, REMIT and EMIR reporting status with the reported identifiers, invoice and settlement links, and the mark-to-market against the current curve. Captured in Sourcing, Hedging and Procurement (srcg) and valued by Portfolio Position and Risk Analytics (risk).
assets.businessMeaning: The cost side of portfolio gross margin per MWh: hedge coverage and hedge cost per segment decide whether propositions are priced above or below what the portfolio actually paid.
assets.accessScope: trading, sourcing, risk and finance staff of the owning portfolio tenant within mandate limits; auditors and ACER or the national regulator for REMIT records; counterparties see only their own confirmations

interfaces.name: hedge transaction api
interfaces.description: Trade capture, confirmation, allocation to segments, mark-to-market, settlement and regulatory-reporting status API used by the sourcing workspace, position and risk analytics, nominations, accounting connectors and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: trade events
interfaces.description: Trade captured, confirmed, amended, reported to ACER, settled and delivery period started events consumed by portfolio position, nominations, risk limits, accounting and dashboards.

interfaces.name: exchange and broker confirmations
interfaces.description: Trade confirmations and settlement statements from exchanges, clearing houses and brokers imported and matched; REMIT and EMIR reports exported to registered reporting mechanisms.

governance.retention: 7 years under fiscal retention; REMIT requires records of wholesale transactions and orders to be kept at least 5 years; PPA documents kept for the contract term plus 7 years
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with counterparties, exchanges, clearing houses, reporting mechanisms and the tenant's accounting; visible only within the owning tenant's trading and risk functions; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Price Curve
assets.description: Market prices and the forward curves derived from them: EPEX spot day-ahead prices in 15-minute blocks since 30 September 2025 and hourly before, intraday continuous and auction prices, ETPA prices, TenneT imbalance and regulation prices per settlement period, EEX and ICE Endex futures settlements per month, quarter and year, TTF and MIBGAS gas prices, OMIE day-ahead (15-minute products since the SDAC change of 30 September 2025) and intraday prices for Spain and Portugal, guarantee-of-origin prices, currency rates, the constructed forward curves per commodity and market with shape factors for profiles and peak and off-peak blocks, the pricing curves published internally for propositions and B2B quotes with validity windows, and the snapshot history so any quote, contract price or valuation can be traced to the curve it used. Built and published by Price Curves and Market Data (pric) and consumed by Proposition and Tariff Builder (prod), B2B Quoting and Cost-Plus Pricing (quot), Portfolio Position and Risk Analytics (risk) and Customer Trading Desk and Click Contracts (ctrd).
assets.businessMeaning: The reference every price in the business is derived from, from a household dynamic tariff to a multi-site hedge; a stale or wrong curve misprices everything at once.
assets.accessScope: pricing, trading, risk and product staff of tenants; published market indices redistributed only within exchange data-licence terms; internal pricing curves visible only to the owning tenant; dynamic-tariff prices shown to end customers in the portal

interfaces.name: price curve api
interfaces.description: Market price query per market, product and period, forward curve and snapshot retrieval, shape factor and pricing-curve publication API used by propositions, quoting, customer trading, risk analytics, forecasting, intraday steering, billing of dynamic tariffs and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: market price events
interfaces.description: Day-ahead auction results published, intraday price updated, futures settlement received, forward curve rebuilt and pricing curve published events consumed by propositions, quoting, position valuation, steering and dashboards.

interfaces.name: market data feeds
interfaces.description: Scheduled price and settlement files and streams from EPEX, ETPA, TenneT, EEX, ICE Endex, OMIE, MIBGAS and weather providers landed and normalised into the time-series store.

governance.retention: market prices kept indefinitely as reference data within licence terms; curve snapshots used for quotes, contracts and valuations kept 7 years with the records they priced
governance.sharingPolicy: raw exchange data redistributed only per the exchange licence; the tenant's own pricing curves never shared between tenants; dynamic-tariff prices derived from public indices shown to customers

assets.name: Portfolio Position
assets.description: The consolidated view of a portfolio per segment and delivery period: contracted sales volumes from supply contracts and executed customer trades, forecast consumption and production, hedged volumes and open exposure, hedge coverage ratio, weighted purchase cost and expected sales revenue, mark-to-market value against the current curve, realised and unrealised margin, volume and price risk measures (value at risk, stress scenarios, churn and weather sensitivity), counterparty credit exposure, the position limits per desk and mandate, the 15-minute financial insight per segment on delivery days, and the daily position snapshot history. Computed by Portfolio Position and Risk Analytics (risk) from contracts, trades, forecasts and prices, and used by Nominations and Position Management (nomi), Gas Shipping and Trading (gass) and Sourcing, Hedging and Procurement (srcg).
assets.businessMeaning: The answer to 'track positions, spot risks, take action': gross margin per MWh and hedge coverage per segment are read from here, and every sourcing and nomination decision starts here.
assets.accessScope: portfolio managers, traders, risk and finance leadership of the owning portfolio tenant and the BRP-as-a-Service desk for managed portfolios; segment views restricted per desk mandate

interfaces.name: portfolio position api
interfaces.description: Position, exposure, coverage, valuation, margin and risk-measure query per portfolio, segment and period with limit checks, used by the portfolio workspace, sourcing, nominations, gas shipping, quoting, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: position and risk events
interfaces.description: Position snapshot published, coverage below target, limit breached, margin deviation and valuation rebuilt events consumed by sourcing, nominations, workflow alerts and leadership dashboards.

governance.retention: daily snapshots kept 7 years because margin and valuation figures feed financial statements and managed-BRP invoicing; intraday snapshots kept 3 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the owning tenant's trading, risk and finance functions; managed clients see their own portfolio; never shared between tenants

subGroups.name: Customer Trading
subGroups.description: The Jules heritage: business customers who trade and manage their own energy within a framework contract, and the site-level consumption profiles and forecasts they and their supplier work from.

assets.name: Customer Trade
assets.description: A trade executed by or for a business customer under a framework supply contract: click and tranche purchases of baseload or peak volumes for future months, quarters or years at the offered price derived from the forward curve plus the contracted mark-up, sell-backs and unwinds, flexible-volume adjustments, spot exposure elections, and flexibility offers from the customer's batteries, CHP or curtailable load; each with the customer, contract and sites, the trader or self-service user and mandate check, the quoted and executed price with curve snapshot, volume and delivery period, the acceptance timestamp and confirmation document, the hedge the supplier placed against it, and the effect on the customer's covered ratio and average price. Executed and confirmed by Customer Trading Desk and Click Contracts (ctrd) against the supply contract and price curve.
assets.businessMeaning: The self-service that keeps large customers: the industrial energy manager can lock prices within its own framework without a phone call, and the supplier hedges the click back to back.
assets.accessScope: the customer's authorised energy manager and traders within their mandate; the supplier's customer-trading desk and portfolio staff; brokers with a mandate; confirmations shared with the customer

interfaces.name: customer trade api
interfaces.description: Price request, click, confirm, unwind, coverage and average-price API with mandate checks, used by the customer-trading portal, the supplier trading desk, sourcing, billing and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: customer trade events
interfaces.description: Price offered, trade clicked, trade confirmed, hedge placed, coverage target reached and delivery started events consumed by portfolio position, sourcing, contracts, billing and customer notifications.

governance.retention: kept for the contract term plus 7 years under fiscal retention; wholesale-linked trades meeting REMIT thresholds kept at least 5 years as transaction records
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the customer and its mandated broker; the supplier's back-to-back hedge stays with the supplier; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Consumption Profile
assets.description: The analysed consumption and production behaviour of a site, connection or customer group: aggregated interval data per 15 minutes, hour, day and month, load duration curves, peak demand and capacity utilisation, weekday and seasonal patterns, temperature and production-volume normalisation, the standard profile category for non-interval connections, self-consumption and feed-in of on-site solar or CHP, flexibility potential of batteries and curtailable load, benchmark comparison with similar sites, the customer-submitted and machine-generated forecasts per site, projected annual costs under the current and alternative products, and anomaly flags. Built by Consumption Analysis and Forecast Self-Service (cons) from meter readings and used by B2B Quoting and Cost-Plus Pricing (quot) and Portfolio Forecasting (fcst).
assets.businessMeaning: What the industrial energy manager, the quoting desk and the forecaster all need from the same readings: understanding per site is the basis of a correct quote, a good forecast and a lower energy cost per unit of production.
assets.accessScope: the customer's energy manager for its own sites; quoting, forecasting and customer-trading staff of the owning supplier tenant; household profiles shown to the household only and aggregated for segment analysis

interfaces.name: consumption profile api
interfaces.description: Profile, load curve, peak, normalisation, forecast submission, cost projection and benchmark API per site and period, used by the customer-trading portal, quoting, forecasting, the customer portal and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: consumption profile events
interfaces.description: Profile rebuilt, anomaly detected, customer forecast submitted and flexibility potential updated events consumed by forecasting, quoting, steering and customer notifications.

interfaces.name: consumption exports
interfaces.description: Site and portfolio consumption reports and interval exports in CSV or Excel for customers, energy audits and sustainability reporting.

governance.retention: site profiles kept for the customer relationship plus 3 years for quoting and forecasting; household-level profiles follow the meter-reading retention and aggregation rules under Dutch smart-meter privacy
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the customer for its own sites and with its mandated consultants; anonymised segment profiles may feed cross-tenant benchmarks and grid-operator data products; never shared at site level between tenants

rootGroups.name: Market and Platform Data
rootGroups.description: The exchanges with the market and the foundation every tenant runs on: the market messages that carry switches, readings, allocations and register updates between suppliers, grid operators, BRPs, TenneT and the Iberian distributors and REE; regulatory reports and the analytics datasets that produce them; and the tenant, workflow and integration data that keeps 50+ energy companies isolated and integrated on one platform.

subGroups.name: Market Communication
subGroups.description: Every message exchanged with the Dutch and Iberian market parties, in the raw form it was sent or received and the processed state the business processes act on.

assets.name: Market Message
assets.description: A message exchanged between the tenant and a market party: Dutch EDSN messages for switching, move-in and move-out, master-data and register updates, meter-reading requests and responses, allocation and reconciliation publications, disconnection and reconnection requests and the TenneT MMC-Hub exchanges introduced with Allocation 2.0; Iberian SIPS consultations, ATR files with distributors (C1, C2, A3, B1, M1, P1/P2 measurement, F1 access-tariff invoices, R1 claims), OMIE and REE settlement and measurement files; each with direction, message type and process code, sender and receiver market-party identifiers (EAN-13 party codes in the Netherlands, distributor and comercializador codes in Iberia), the connection point and process instance it belongs to, the raw payload as sent or received, validation and acknowledgement state, retries and technical errors, the processed business result, and the transport timestamps against the code-defined response terms. Routed and archived by Dutch Market Messaging Hub (mcom) and Iberian Market Communication (imcm), and consumed by Switching and Move-In Market Processes (swch).
assets.businessMeaning: The market's audit trail: what was sent to whom and when decides switch disputes, allocation disputes and compliance with the information code, and it is the input for 20 million connections processed daily.
assets.accessScope: market-communication operators of the owning tenant and the platform's market-communication team for technical support; business processes consume processed results; raw payloads visible only to market-communication and support roles

interfaces.name: market message api
interfaces.description: Send, receive, validate, acknowledge, retry, search and trace API per process, connection and message type with response-term monitoring, used by switching, meter data, allocation, debtor management, care and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: market message events
interfaces.description: Message received, validated, rejected, acknowledged, response overdue and process result available events consumed by switching, register mirror, meter data, allocation, workflow exceptions and dashboards.

interfaces.name: market message payloads
interfaces.description: Raw XML, EDIFACT and CSV payloads exchanged with EDSN, the MMC-Hub, grid operators, SIPS, ATR distributors, OMIE and REE, archived immutably with transport receipts.

governance.retention: messages and receipts kept 7 years because market disputes, reconciliation and fiscal audits are settled on the message trail; raw payloads archived immutably
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged only with the addressed market party through the certified market interfaces; each tenant sees only its own messages; the platform operator's market-communication team accesses payloads for support under processor agreements

subGroups.name: Data and Insight
subGroups.description: The reports the regulators, TSOs and auditors demand, and the curated datasets behind them and behind the operational dashboards.

assets.name: Regulatory Report
assets.description: A filed or filable report required by a regulator, system operator or statutory scheme: ACM supply-licence and consumer-protection reporting (complaint statistics, switching and disconnection figures, price-cap and model-contract compliance), Belastingdienst energy-tax returns per bracket and connection count (ODE included since 2023), VertiCer (CertiQ) and CNMC GdO guarantee-of-origin cancellations and the annual fuel-mix disclosure, TenneT and GTS BRP and shipper compliance reports, REMIT transaction and fundamental-data reports to ACER, CNMC and ERSE supply and complaint reporting, Spanish electricity-tax and bono social reporting, CSRD and energy-saving obligation extracts, and the internal audit evidence; each with the reporting period, the analytics dataset and version it was produced from, the produced document and submission file, reviewer and approval, filing date and receipt, and correction and resubmission history. Produced by Regulatory Reporting and Compliance (regs).
assets.businessMeaning: Where compliance incidents become visible or are prevented: the report must be reproducible from the underlying data, filed on time, and defensible in a regulator's inspection.
assets.accessScope: compliance, finance and leadership of the owning tenant; regulators and auditors receive the filed reports; the platform's data-and-insight team maintains the report definitions

interfaces.name: regulatory report api
interfaces.description: Report definition, generation, review, approval, filing-status and resubmission API used by the compliance workspace, workflow deadlines, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: regulatory report events
interfaces.description: Report generated, review due, approved, filed, receipt received and correction required events consumed by workflow deadlines, leadership dashboards and audit trails.

interfaces.name: regulatory filings
interfaces.description: Submission files and documents in the format each regulator or scheme requires (XML, XBRL, CSV, PDF) and the receipts returned.

governance.retention: filed reports and their source dataset versions kept 7 years under fiscal retention, 5 years for REMIT records and longer where a licence condition requires; never deleted while a regulator inspection is open
governance.sharingPolicy: filed with the addressed regulator, TSO or scheme; visible to the owning tenant's compliance and leadership; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Analytics Dataset
assets.description: A curated, versioned dataset in the platform's warehouse built from the operational assets: connection and customer counts per product, segment and grid area, straight-through billing and correction rates, invoice ageing and collection, contact and self-service rates, forecast accuracy, nomination timeliness, allocation reconciliation accuracy, imbalance cost per MWh, hedge coverage and gross margin per MWh and per connection, the 15-minute financial insight per segment, propositions launched and campaign conversion, tenant usage and platform health, plus anonymised cross-tenant benchmark tables; each with lineage to source assets, refresh cadence, quality checks, row-level tenant keys and the pseudonymisation applied. Built and served by Operational Dashboards and Analytics (dash) and used by Regulatory Reporting and Compliance (regs).
assets.businessMeaning: Where every north-star KPI in this domain is read: one trusted set of numbers per tenant, from proposition manager to director, on the same data as billing and settlement.
assets.accessScope: analysts, operations managers and leadership of the owning tenant per row-level tenant key and role; pseudonymised for analysts; cross-tenant benchmarks only in anonymised aggregate; the platform's data-and-insight team maintains models

interfaces.name: analytics query api
interfaces.description: Semantic-layer query, KPI, drill-down and export API with tenant and role scoping, used by dashboards, regulatory reporting, the portfolio workspace, the customer portal insight widgets and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: dataset refresh events
interfaces.description: Dataset refreshed, quality check failed, KPI threshold crossed and benchmark published events consumed by dashboards, workflow alerts and regulatory reporting.

interfaces.name: analytics exports
interfaces.description: Scheduled extracts to tenants' BI tools and finance systems in CSV or Parquet, and anonymised benchmark exports.
